pageContent.markdown:
92 Southampton Row, Holborn, London WC1

# DoubleTree by Hilton London – West End

Guest room wallcoverings at the Holborn hotel, the former Bonnington, through the main works of 2019: two full floors, 30 rooms and their corridors, finished while the hotel stayed open.

![The DoubleTree by Hilton London – West End on Southampton Row, Holborn: the red-brick and stone frontage, seen from the street.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/doubletree-west-end-commons-01.jpg)

The hotel on Southampton Row, 2024. Venue photograph, not our work. Photograph: Frombowen / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0).

## Project record

Client, materials & project facts

**Client**
: DoubleTree by Hilton London – West End

**Designer**
: –Not recorded

**Main contractor**
: –Not recorded

**Maker and paper**
: –Not recorded

**Area or rooms**
: 30 rooms on two floors, while the hotel stayed open (2019)

**Scope**
: Guest room wallcoverings

**Year**
: 2019

## At a glance

- **Hotel:** DoubleTree by Hilton London – West End
- **Address:** 92 Southampton Row, Holborn
- **Years on site:** main works in 2019
- **Scope:** guest room wallcoverings; in 2019, levels 5 and 6, 30 rooms and their corridors, while the hotel stayed open on the other floors
- **Formerly:** the Bonnington Hotel

## The work

The commission was the guest rooms. Pattern, batch and the order of rooms were agreed before the first length was cut, so a repeated room could stay consistent down a corridor.

In July 2019 we completed levels 5 and 6: 30 Premium and Deluxe rooms and their corridors. The hardest part was working in a hotel that was still open, with guests on the other floors. We first worked here in December 2017, hanging Tektura wide vinyl.

The first photographs on this page show the Southampton Row building from the street, before and after it took the DoubleTree name. They show the building, not the finished rooms. The rest are our own photographs of the finished rooms and corridors.

## Next step

For a similar guest-room package, send the room types, the programme and who supplies the material; a survey then decides preparation, quantities and the order of rooms.

## Photographs on this page

The first three are photographs of the building, two of them by the photographers credited below. They show the building, not our work.

The others are our own photographs of the finished rooms and corridors, first posted on our Instagram, [@mrwallcover](https://www.instagram.com/mrwallcover/): one from December 2017 ([see the post](https://www.instagram.com/p/BdNpAgPArnf/)) and the rest from 19 July 2019 ([see the post](https://www.instagram.com/p/B0GpM3Vlmkh/)), the post that records the 30 rooms on levels 5 and 6.

- The hotel on Southampton Row, 2024: photograph by Frombowen, [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:DoubleTree_by_Hilton_Hotel_London_-_West_End.jpg). Resized for the web.
- The former Bonnington Hotel, now the DoubleTree, 2026: photograph by APK, [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0), via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:DoubleTree_by_Hilton_-_Southampton_Row,_London.jpg). Resized for the web.

## Photographs

How the commission ran

## The same standards, on every commission.

Each commission has a written scope by room, walls prepared until they are true, protected floors, batch and shade control, set-out from the room’s focal points, and a return visit. [Read the method](https://www.mrwallcover.com/practice/#method).

The six standards in full

01

### Survey and scope, room by room

We measure the wall that will actually be hung, allow for the repeat and the wastage, and write a scope of works room by room before anyone orders paper.

02

### Preparation decides the finish

Walls are filled, made good and primed until they are true. If a wall is not ready for the material specified, we say so before the last drop is ordered.

03

### Protection and containment

Floors, furniture and finished joinery are protected as part of the hang. Work is contained and the place is left tidy each evening. In a home we are visitors; in a hotel we work around the house.

04

### Batch and shade control

Deliveries are checked against the measure, and batches and shading are managed so that a corridor of rooms reads as one surface.

05

### Set out from the room's focal points

Pattern is set out from chimneypieces, doorcases and bed walls, so the pattern sits square to the cornice and the joinery.

06

### One team, then the return visit

The people who start are the people who finish. Four to six weeks after completion we come back to look at every seam and edge, and the workmanship is guaranteed for twelve months.

[See the finish up close: seams, internal corners, edges and joins from our own installations](https://www.mrwallcover.com/details/)

By [Dorin Burcus](https://www.mrwallcover.com/about/#dorin), founder · Last updated 22 October 2026
